correctness.rationale: For an interior oracle the bounded log-growth score satisfies \(P h_{\lambda^\star}=0\) and the exact information identity \(\operatorname{Var}(h_{\lambda^\star})=P h_{\lambda^\star}^2=-M''(\lambda^\star)=J\). A local score equation, exponentially small boundary-event control, and bounded-summand moment bounds yield the asymptotic normal law and second/third moment limits. Taylor expansion then gives the one-step expected regret constant \(1/2\); harmonic summation gives cumulative \(\tfrac12\log N+o(\log N)\). A fixed MDP component perturbs the score by uniformly \(O(n^{-1})\), so it does not alter the leading law. The deterministic Bernoulli checker independently confirms the coefficient in exactly summed finite-sample examples.

value.rationale: The result answers a specifically identified theoretical gap in GRAPA regret analysis and sharpens the 2026 Bayes-assisted MDP guarantee from a generic cumulative \(O(\sqrt N)\) consequence to the exact logarithmic leading order under a natural interior regime. The prior-neutral leading coefficient gives a concrete design interpretation: any fixed amount of prior predictive mass can change finite-sample behavior without paying second-order asymptotic oracle regret. The null corollary also quantifies expected bankruptcy speed, complementing qualitative almost-sure bankruptcy results.
